title: One-night stand tour with Benny Carter
summary: Her only tour of one-night stands; six weeks from July from New York as far south and to Detroit.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: Yeah, well after "If I Had A Ribbon Bow", "Who Is Sylvia", "Molly Malone", and "Barbara Allen", which were, I supposed, the height of our classic approach in the repertoire, that relationship didn't last too long because our next session coming up is "Lock Lomond" again, "Just Like A Gypsy", "My Blue Heaven" and "St. Louis Blues", which were made for Decca.
That's right, under your name.
Yes, under my name.
But in-between you've

Oh yeah, yeah, yeah. Well I did a tour of one-night stands with Benny Carter. And at the end of the tour, he had a record session. And we sort of stayed up all night recording these things. This was the first -- well, not actually, because if you want to say a big band, the first one was with John Kirby -- I mean with Claude Thornhill, the very beginning. But this was my first big band recording session. It was Benny's session, but he asked me to sing a couple of selections on it.
Very refreshing kind of change, too, from some of the other materials.
Yeah, well --
You didn't have the uniform backing every time.
Yeah, well Benny Carter is a terrific arranger. He picks out these things very good. It was a very good experience being out on

the road with Benny.
It was the only time I had ever gone
out on the road doing one night stands. He did a
beautiful job.

We did twenty-three states in six
weeks.

That's how long you were
with the band altogether?

Yeah. Just for that
one tour, that one tour.

We were booked out of New York in July,
and we were out for six weeks. We went as far south
as Natchez, Mississippi, Shreveport, Louisiana.

We came up and played through Chicago,
Detroit and all that, then back to New York.

I often wonder how the singers like
Ella Fitzgerald held up under these one-nighters,
because it was quite a strain.

Of course, I didn't ride in the bus. I
had my own car. And I had a driver, but some of our
jumps were like seven-hundred miles.
